To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
GalnPAs/InP heterostructures are promising for the fabrication of injection lasers and diode emitters emitting in the 0.9–1.3µ range.
the life of GalnP/lnP heterostuctures is limited by the degradation of the active region.
GalnPAs/InP heterostructures can be used in the 1–1.5 µ range in high-power diodes and lasers for a period in excess of 2000 h.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of degradation processes in GalnPAs/InP heterostructures and the development of methods for their life prediction.
the development of new types of injection lasers and light-emitting diodes with high reliability and long life.
the study of degradation of GalnPAs-based heterostructures and devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GalnPAs/InP heterostructures have a high potential for use in lasers and diodes operating in the 1-µ region.
the GalnPAs/InP heterostructures are very promising for use in high-power diode lasers.
GalnPAs/InP heterostructures are very stable at the current density of 3–4 kA/cm2 and the temperature of 25 °C, and that their stability decreases with increasing temperature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lifetime of GalnPAs heterostructures is not limited at the present stage of development of the technology of epitaxial growth.
the life tests of GalnPAs heterostructures at room and medium temperatures have shown that the lifetime is not limited by degradation of the active region.

the service life of GalnP/lnP heterojunctions is not limited by the degradation of the heterojunctions themselves, but is determined by the degradation of ohmic contacts to the p-GaAs substrate and the GaAs/AlGaAs heterojunction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the life of GalnPAl/lnP heterojunctions is limited not by the diffusion of impurity atoms but rather by the diffusion of point defects.
the service life of GalnPAlnP heterostructures in diode structures can be extended by a factor of two or more if the temperature of the ambient medium is lowered by 20–40 °C.
GalnPAs/InP heterostructures can be operated in the temperature range 25–80°C with a current density of 3–5kA/cm2 for 2000h without degradation.
